trust_decision.summary: When a K8s NetworkPolicy ingress peer is translated into Cilium L3 selectors, a peer that has only an ipBlock must produce only a CIDR selector. The cluster-name injection must not turn the absent podSelector into a selector that matches the whole local namespace. This is decided in parseNetworkPolicyPeer and in the ingress loop of ParseNetworkPolicy.

landing_point.why: The summary names NetworkPolicy, ipBlock and ingress from the local namespace. The only K8s NetworkPolicy peer translator is parseNetworkPolicyPeer and its ingress caller in the same file.

fix_sites.entry_point: k8s.ParseNetworkPolicy (public Go API). The agent reaches it through the NetworkPolicy watcher in pkg/policy/k8s/network_policy.go:22. The early-return guard was ALREADY PRESENT at the pinned commit (pkg/k8s/network_policy.go:112).
fix_sites.module_kind: core policy translation (same file as landing point)

fix_sites.entry_point: k8s.ParseNetworkPolicy -> parseNetworkPolicyPeer (refactor: the peer parser now returns Selectors and handles ipBlock itself)
k8s.ParseNetworkPolicy egress To loop (refactor only; the egress path was already guarded at pkg/k8s/network_policy.go:216)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: No O2 site or O8 route exists. The pinned tree already carries the guard at pkg/k8s/network_policy.go:112, so there is nothing left to dismiss.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Peers that combine podSelector with namespaceSelector, and peers with only a podSelector under a configured cluster name, must still get the cluster label and the local-namespace label. An empty From list must stay a wildcard.

O6_input_shapes: ingress peer with ipBlock only, clusterName set (not PolicyAnyCluster)
ingress peer with ipBlock only, clusterName = PolicyAnyCluster
empty peer {} (refactor commit 1c84ae3 maps it to the local namespace)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The egress To loop calls parseNetworkPolicyPeer without the outer selector-nil guard at line 216. It would then inherit the same cluster-label-on-nil-podSelector widening if the function guard were removed.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The ingress and egress loops are near-duplicates that have already drifted apart (the guard at line 216 exists only on egress). A maintainer could plausibly drop or reorder one of the guards. This is still a WHERE-type sibling in the same file.

O9_family: CWE-863 incorrect authorization: a policy translation that over-widens a peer selector (an ipBlock-only peer also matches the local namespace)

O10_build.toolchain: Go toolchain per go.mod; dependencies are vendored (vendor/)
O10_build.project_tests: pkg/k8s/network_policy_test.go (TestParseNetworkPolicy, TestParseNetworkPolicyNoSelectors, Test_parseNetworkPolicyPeer); these are pure unit tests

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add an early `return nil` in parseNetworkPolicyPeer when both selectors are nil. That is exactly the published fix, and it is already present at the pinned commit (pkg/k8s/network_policy.go:112).

out_of_scope_notes: The pinned commit 6b93e7a is titled 'fix: Fix wildcard namespace bypass for selectorless ipBlock rules'. It already contains bacea640's guard (pkg/k8s/network_policy.go:112) and its regression test loop (pkg/k8s/network_policy_test.go:525). So the vulnerable behaviour is absent at the pin. The remaining commit, 1c84ae3, is a refactor plus an empty-peer semantics change.
cilium-cli/clustermesh/clustermesh.go:1864-1868 calls ParseNetworkPolicy from the CLI; it is a consumer, not a separate implementation.
unverified: That 6b93e7a is a cherry-pick or equivalent of bacea640 is inferred from the commit title and the matching code and test content, not from git metadata.
Whether the empty-peer change in 1c84ae3 has security weight was not assessed. At the pin, an empty peer yields nil L3, which selects nothing per pkg/policy/types/policyentry.go:63-67.
